business.title: Blade-pitch dynamics in DFIG wind turbines: modal sensitivity, transient loading, and weak-grid feasibility
business.desc: Small-signal and sub-synchronous stability studies of doubly-fed induction generator (DFIG) wind turbines almost universally treat the blade-pitch angle as a frozen parameter, assuming pitch actuation is too slow to interact with electrical and torsional modes—an assumption widely used but rarely quantified. Using a high-fidelity 24-state model of a 3.6 MW DFIG turbine that retains the fourth-order machine, two-mass drivetrain, rotor- and grid-side converter controls, a phase-locked loop (PLL), and a dynamic pitch controller, this paper compares the modal spectrum and the large-signal response with pitch dynamic versus frozen, across short-circuit ratios (SCR) from $$\approx 43$$ to $$\approx 3$$ and the pitch-active wind range. Pitch dynamics shift the damping of every electrical, network, converter, and torsional mode by less than $$1\times 10^{-3}$$, and the corresponding eigenvalue, modal frequency and mode-shape deviations remain below $${2\times 10^{-3}}$$ (relative), $${4\times 10^{-4}}\,\textrm{Hz}$$ and $${1.1}^\circ $$ respectively, justifying frozen pitch specifically for modal and sub-synchronous resonance screening and for impedance-based screening, but not for large-disturbance, overload, voltage-recovery or thermal/mechanical-limit assessment. The sustained large-signal response, however, is strongly pitch dependent: for a finite-rate wind ramp to rated-plus conditions, freezing pitch leaves a sustained power overload of up to $$54\%$$ of rated apparent power, held indefinitely, and a depressed weak-grid point-of-common-coupling (PCC) voltage that dynamic pitch removes; a voltage-dip ride-through swept over dip depth and duration confirms the dual—fast grid-side transients are pitch-invariant. The discriminant is disturbance duration relative to the pitch time constant, and a parametric study places the transition at $$T_d/T_\beta \approx {0.3}$$. A weak-grid sweep further shows the feasibility limit of this configuration to be a voltage-loadability (PV-nose) limit near SCR $$\approx $$ 2.3 rather than a damping limit, extendable to SCR $$\approx $$ 1.7 by converter reactive support. Modeling refinements for a well-posed PLL equilibrium and a consistent network coupling are also documented, and the frozen-pitch reduction is shown to cut eigenvalue and sweep cost by 25–$${30}\%$$.

technology.title: Extended physics-informed neural networks (Ex-PINNs): a machine-learning method for solving partial differential equations in domain with spatially heterogeneous parameters
technology.desc: In this paper, we propose a machine-learning based method called Extended Physics-informed Neural Networks (Ex-PINNs) to solve the partial differential equations in domain with unknown parameters. In the existing PINNs, the partial differential equations with distributed parameters are often solved by setting several sub-domains, which can be cumbersome when many interfaces and sub-domains must be prescribed. In order to solve such problem, an extra neural network is introduced to the standard PINN architecture for the characterization and reconstruction of the unknown continuous parameters. The loss function of the Ex-PINNs consists of residual part and boundary condition part formulated by not only the neural networks of solution, but also the one characterizing the parameters. By the method, we avoid the need for standard PINNs to introduce a large number of interfaces and sub-domains to approximate solution. We also present the solid mechanics and the heat conduction problems for the validation of the proposed Ex-PINN. Numerical experiments show that the results of the Ex-PINNs are in good agreement with the FEM in relative error of less than 3.0%. The method provides an extension of PINN in latent cases such as solid mechanics.

world.title: Foreign Researchers Hail Ethiopia’s Green Legacy Initiative as a Model for Environmental Conservation
world.desc:
Addis Ababa, September 19, 2026 (ENA) —Foreign forestry researchers have praised Ethiopia’s Green Legacy Initiative as an outstanding example of environmental conservation, citing its wide-ranging contribution to climate action and food security.
It was learned that Ethiopia has planted a total of 56.2 billion seedlings, further strengthening the country’s leadership in efforts to restore and protect natural resources.
According to the foreign researchers interviewed by ENA, the initiative is not only helping Ethiopia lay the groundwork for greater resilience in food production and long-term sustainability, but is also addressing the impacts of global climate change.
Dutch researcher Albert Schenk described the initiative as a practical demonstration of Ethiopia’s contribution to the fight against climate change.
He said Ethiopia’s Green Legacy Initiative is an impressive model for development and urged other countries to support similar efforts.
Schenk emphasized that protecting forests and natural resources is essential to building a climate-resilient economy, and argued that investment in green development delivers returns worthy of sustained attention.
Ugandan forest resource development researcher Robert Atugonza said Ethiopia is pursuing ambitious forestry and natural resource protection plans while delivering tangible results.
He added that the initiative continues to serve as a foundation for climate mitigation, environmental protection, and food security.
He urged other African countries, particularly in East Africa, to learn from Ethiopia’s approach and maintain momentum through collective effort.
Tanzania-based forestry protection program coordinator Almas Kashindye described Ethiopia’s sustained seedling planting and care efforts as a remarkable public initiative.
He noted that protecting and nurturing natural resources offers multiple benefits, including safeguarding biodiversity and water bodies, while supporting climate mitigation and food security.
Bolivian scholar Humberto Gómez Cerveró, the Thematic Lead on Participatory Forest Restoration and Programme Coordinator at Tropenbos International also praised Ethiopia’s citizens for their contributions, noting that the seedlings planted in recent years carry significant value for ongoing global climate efforts.
The researchers said the initiative reflects a comprehensive development strategy that has achieved notable success in a short period.
